title: API authentication requirements not exposed in catalog, spec, or operation details
description: The test API requires an X-API-Key header for authentication, but this requirement is not discoverable through any of the standard API discovery mechanisms. The API catalog view, operation inspect command, and OpenAPI spec all lack security scheme information. Users can only discover the credential type by examining audit events after making a request.
reproduction_steps: Run `jentic inspect <operation-id>` for the test API operation
Run `jentic apis spec jentic-test/test-api/1.0.0` and examine the OpenAPI spec
Note that none of these show securitySchemes or authentication requirements
expected_behavior: The API catalog, operation details, or OpenAPI spec should indicate what authentication the API requires (e.g., X-API-Key header, OAuth, etc.) so developers can understand credential requirements before making requests.
actual_behavior: No authentication requirements are shown in the catalog view, inspect output, or OpenAPI spec. The spec has no securitySchemes defined. Authentication type is only discoverable by checking audit events after execution.
evidence: API detail view doesn't show authentication requirements (e.g., which headers are needed)
The spec has no `securitySchemes` or security requirements defined, even though the setup instructions mention the API requires an `X-API-Key` header
Only discoverable through the event log's `credential.accessed` event showing `wire_type: api_key`
